World Energy Day: Ensuring Access to Sustainable Energy for All 🔋💡

With today, as World Energy Day, marked as a time to reflect on “energy efficiency and production alternatives”, it is also important to consider how we, as a global community, recognize the value and importance of sustainable energy.

The COP28 UAE Consensus to Triple Renewable capacity and Double Efficiency by 2030 sets out a clear agenda. Yet at the core of these developments are communities and people — those who still lack their fundamental right to sustainable energy.⚡️

Today, nearly:

➡️ 1.18 billion people live in energy poverty.

➡️ 685 million people live without electricity access.

➡️ 2.1 billion people lacking access to fundamental clean cooking facilities.

➡️ 2 billion people live in conflict-affected areas where energy security is critical.

➡️ Nearly 1 billion people in the Global South lack electricity in healthcare facilities.

As countries update their NDCs for COP30, and the G20 presidency seeks to mobilize finance for a just energy transition, 2025 presents a critical opportunity to move from intent to impactful action.
 
We need to ensure that resources are accessible, strategically allocated, and equitably distributed to those who need them most. Sustainable energy is not only a component of the SDG7 Agenda —“Ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable, and modern energy for all” — it is also a key enabler of the entire 2030 Agenda. 🌐
